messages:
maya: heads-up — i'm landing an auto-triage change for SAST rules today: auto-suppress if FP rate > 90%, require human review if FP rate between 70-90%. asking: will KMS key rotation break our ability to unmute or re-evaluate suppressed findings?

sam: quick q — if we accidentally suppress a real vuln, what's the rollback path? can we force-unmute per-pr or per-finding?

alex: there is an evidence_override endpoint but it needs the scan-keystore key to unwrap artifacts. if the key gets rotated and old key versions removed, the service can't unwrap older blobs. so rotation policy matters.

scanner-bot: SAST run #456 completed — 12 findings (3 auto-suppressed by rule fp_rate=0.92). results: https://ci.redwood/scan/456 :eyes: 

lia: we should definitely emit an audit event every time suppression happens: suppression.reason, rule_fp_rate, rule_version, changed_by (if manual), key_version (unwrap attempt). compliance wants traceability. retention: they asked for 1y retention yesterday.

maya: exactly. proposal: 1) emit audit log entry on suppression 2) include key_version used to decrypt evidence (or null if no decrypt) 3) keep evidence rewraps for 1 year. question for infra: feasible? @alex

alex: feasible. my preferred approach: envelope encryption + key-version metadata on blobs. when rotation happens we keep previous key-versions available for unwrap for N days (grace window). also add a rewrap hook so CI can re-encrypt artifacts under the new key version on rotation. pseudocode: 

`````
# rotation hook (sketch)
wrapped=$(kms wrap --key project/ci-key --data artifact.enc)
curl -X POST https://scans.redwood.internal/internal/rewrap -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" -d "wrapped=$wrapped&key_version=$NEW_KEY_VERSION"
`````

If the scan service stores key_version alongside artifact, we can always attempt unwrap with that version chain.

sam: also: add an emergency override that is auditable. e.g. endpoint /override with required approval header that writes to audit log and notifies oncall. must be gated.

oncall: if an override leads to an actual missed vuln -> incident runbook: 1) set thresholds back, 2) run full rescan across affected repos, 3) notify owners + security pager, 4) open incident channel #inc-scan-<ts>. runbook draft exists at /runbooks/scan-miss.md.

lia: can we include the suppression event in our central audit stream (log sinks -> BigQuery / SIEM)? otherwise searching for suppressed-but-unwrapped evidence will be hard.

maya: yep — plan is to push audit events to the audit sink with these fields: event_type=sast.suppression, rule_id, fp_rate, suppressed_by (auto|user), key_version, artifact_id, repo, pr. i'll add schema in the PR.

alex: test plan i suggest: 
- unit test wrap/unwrap with multiple key versions
- CI integration test: simulate rotation (promote new version, keep old) and run scanner to unwrap old artifacts
- e2e: force a suppression, then call override endpoint and confirm audit record + notification
- compliance check: query audit sink and validate 1-year retention TTL

sam: do we need a migration for existing suppressed findings to add key_version metadata?

alex: yes — small backfill job: iterate suppressed findings with artifact reference, try to fetch metadata, record key_version if present. if no artifact, mark key_version=null. backfill should be idempotent.

maya: i'll open a PR that adds the audit schema + the suppression flag to the findings model and wire up the rotation hook. @alex please add the rewrap endpoint sketch to the PR. tagging security-ops for a dry run (Wed 10am).

scanner-bot: scheduled: dry-run of rotation + auto-triage Wednesday 10:00 UTC in #eng-sre. reminder set. :calendar: 

alex: i'll draft tests and post the PR link later today.

maya: thanks all — if anyone has objections to the thresholds, speak now or i'll merge after the dry run results. :thumbsup:
